question_text: Define radius of gyration. Write its relation to the moment of inertia.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The radius of gyration of a body about
an axis is the distance at which the
whole mass, if concentrated as a point,
would have the same moment of inertia.
steps.why: k compresses a whole mass distribution into one honest distance — which is why every disc/ring comparison question speaks in k.
common_mistakes: Defining k as "the radius of the body" — it is a computed distance, not a physical radius.

recall.must_convey: That k is the distance where the whole mass, concentrated, gives the same moment of inertia.
accept: distance where the whole mass concentrated gives the same I

steps.label: The relation
steps.why: The relation is the definition in symbols: replace the body by a point mass M at distance k and demand the same I.
common_mistakes: Writing k = I/M without the square root.

recall.must_convey: That I = Mk², so k = root of I by M.
accept: k is root I by M
reject: distance where the whole mass concentrated gives the same I
